title: Quantized Kernel Canary Matrix and CI Rollout Protocol (v1)
author: Asha Patel
body:
> **Archived 2025-02-10:** this page is superseded by "Quantized Kernel Canary Matrix and CI Deployment Protocol" and is kept for reference only.

Summary:
This page describes how we canary and ship quantized inference kernels across our GPU families. It covers the test matrix (GPU families, quant formats, model archetypes), the CI stages, metric gates, rollout/rollback rules, a Terraform feature-flag example, and an on-call checklist. The aim is to let cheaper quantized kernels reach production without customer-visible latency or correctness regressions.

Audience:
- Runtime engineers building and releasing kernels
- CI/CD and release engineering
- Serving and infra SREs operating canaries
- Platform owners tracking serving cost

Why this exists:
Quantized paths (int8/int4, nf4, dynamic quant) behave differently across A100/H100/L4/RTX hardware. Minor numeric differences or microkernel scheduling changes can cause latency spikes or quality drops for specific prompt shapes. This protocol makes sure kernels are validated across representative workloads in CI and again in a gated staging canary, with clear rollback rules.

Definitions and SLAs:
- Canary run: a staged experiment on a small set of production-like instances using shadowed or sampled real traffic.
- Merge SLO for kernels to master: no P95 latency regression > 15% and no accuracy regression > 1.5% on the canonical eval set for the target archetype.
- Canary SLOs: P50/P95 latency within 10% of baseline, 99.9% successful stream rate on streaming paths, and quality metrics inside configured thresholds.

Quantized Canary Matrix:
| GPU family | Quant modes | Model archetype | Sequence lengths | Notes |
| A100 (PCIe/80GB) | int8, int4, nf4 | 7B causal / chat | 64, 512 | Primary baseline; new kernels validated here first. |
| H100 (HBM3) | int8, nf4 | 34B encoder-decoder | 128, 1024 | Watch KV cache growth and HBM scheduling. |
| L4 / T4 | int8, nf4 | 2B/4B generators | 32, 128 | Cost tier; small-batch tail latency is the main risk. |
| RTX-like (dev fleet) | int8 | dev-only | 8, 32 | Early vector-lane issue detection; never receives canary traffic. |

For each size class choose one canonical model that exercises attention, KV cache and streaming, and keep a small, stable prompt set for it.

CI stages:
1) Per-kernel unit tests; required before artifact publish.
2) Microbench harness for matmul/attention kernels across compiler flags; must be within 5% of golden runs.
3) Emulator integration smoke on the dev docker image to catch API/ABI breaks.
4) Nightly mixed-workload matrix across the full canary matrix on ephemeral sandbox clusters, with telemetry diffs to baseline.
5) Staging canary with 1-5% sampled production-like traffic or shadow traffic.
6) Automated gate check plus a human sign-off window of 30–90 minutes depending on model.
7) Gradual production ramp through the Release Orchestrator once the canary passes.

Automated gates:
- Latency p50/p95/p99 — fail if P95 increase > 15% or P99 increase > 20% over baseline.
- Success rate (no crash, no OOM) — fail if < 99.9%.
- Fixed-batch throughput (tokens/sec) — fail if drop > 15%.
- Quality score on the canonical prompt set — fail if delta < -1.5% (configurable per model).
- Token distribution sanity (unknown token rate, stop-token frequency) — fail on spikes > 5x baseline.
- GPU memory telemetry — fail on sustained allocation growth > 10%.
- Every canary run must be tagged with kernel artifact id, compile flags, CUDA/CUDNN/driver versions and quant profile id.

Rollback:
- Automatic: any gate failure makes the rollout controller shift traffic back to the last-good variant.
- Semi-automatic: degradation in the warning band pages owners and pauses the rollout.
- Manual: on-call or the owner can abort and roll back from the Release Console.

Preflight checklist:
- [ ] Artifact provenance recorded (commit, build id, container digest).
- [ ] Quant profile id stored in the model catalog.
- [ ] Baseline telemetry for the target GPU family captured within the last 7 days.
- [ ] Preemption / slot pressure test executed.
- [ ] Alerts wired to #canary-alerts, the oncall pager and the Release Console.
- [ ] Synthetic prompts and health probes for streaming and non-streaming paths.
- [ ] Single-instance smoke pass on each GPU family.

Terraform feature-flag example:
```hcl
resource "redwood_feature_flag" "quant_kernel_canary" {
  name    = "quant-kernel-canary-${var.artifact_id}"
  project = var.project
  default = 0
  rules = [
    { type = "percentage", value = var.canary_percentage }
  ]
  metadata = {
    kernel_artifact = var.artifact_id
    quant_profile   = var.quant_profile_id
  }
}
```

On-call runbook:
1) Check the Release Console for failing gates, the artifact id and affected GPU family.
2) Pull p50/p95 for the last 5 minutes, GPU memory graphs and OOM/driver errors.
3) If auto-rollback has not fired, roll back from the Release Console and note the action id.
4) If rollback fails, set canary percentage to 0 and route to last-good.
5) Attach reproducer prompts, kernel logs and driver logs; open an incident if more than 1% of traffic is disrupted.
6) Kernel owners reproduce locally with the directed microbench.

Reproducing failures:
- Same GPU family and driver combination, same failing prompt set.
- Same compile flags and quant profile in the microbench.
- Capture Nsight traces or perf counters and diff against baseline.
- For numeric differences, compare against the float fallback path.

Dashboards per canary run: Canary Overview, GPU Family Breakdown, Prompt Set Replay, Canary Event Log.

Retention:
- Full canary traces (histograms and kernel traces) are kept for 30 days; aggregate summaries for 2 years.
- Kernel build artifacts and quant profiles live in the binary artifact registry with immutable IDs.

Ownership:
- Kernel engineering: artifacts and unit tests.
- CI/CD: nightly matrix orchestration.
- Serving SRE: staging canary fleet and gate automation.
- Product economics: production ramp sign-off.

Best practices:
- Begin with short-sequence, small-batch slices before long sequences or bursty traffic.
- Use shadow traffic to compare outputs without user impact.
- Ramp 1% -> 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% with 30–60 minute holds when quality is sensitive.

Known limitations:
- Quant profiles are per GPU family; there is no automatic cross-architecture translation yet.
- L4 small-batch tail latency produces the most false positives.
